title: Probe Privacy Budget and Annotation Retention Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s operational approach to (1) managing privacy budgets for live and synthetic probes, (2) retention policies and purge workflows for annotations and raw probe artifacts, and (3) cost-control guardrails for probe-driven evaluation pipelines. It is intended for ML engineers, evaluators, SRE, and security/compliance reviewers.

Goals

- Protect customer data and limit privacy risk from probes while preserving evaluation fidelity.
- Maintain a clear, auditable retention lifecycle for probe artifacts and annotation datasets.
- Constrain evaluation costs by enforcing budgeted probe storage and annotation spending.
- Provide an operator runbook for retention changes, emergency purges, and privacy incidents.

Scope

- Applies to all probe sources used in the eval harness: shadow traffic probes, synthetic probe farms, and field-captured debug probes.
- Covers raw inputs (payloads, transcripts), derived artifacts (tokenized inputs, embeddings, model outputs), human annotations, and evaluation metrics/telemetry.
- Integrations: Probe ingestion pipeline (probe-ingest), annotation service (annotate-v2), eval-orchestrator, telemetry-warehouse (events-db), and KMS-backed storage.

Key Concepts and Definitions

- Probe: Any request/record used to evaluate model behavior. Includes synthetic seeds, mirrored production calls, and targeted adversarial probes.
- Privacy Budget: A quantified allowance (DP epsilon or equivalent policy) used to bound cumulative privacy exposure for a dataset or customer. We track budgets per-customer (when applicable) and per-probe-catalog.
- Annotation TTL: Time-to-live for label data and raw artifacts before automatic purging.

Policy Summary (defaults)

1) Privacy budget regime:
   - Live customer-shadow probes: treat as customer data; default policy: do NOT retain raw payload beyond 72 hours without explicit opt-in. Apply aggregation/minimization and register to customer’s privacy budget.
   - Production-mirrored probes (anonymized): retain for 30 days by default, subject to DP noise injection if aggregated exports leave the secure environment.
   - Synthetic probe farms: no customer PII expected; default retention for raw probe generation seeds is 365 days.

2) Annotation retention and classification:
   - Raw artifacts (audio, full request bodies): default TTL = 30 days for non-sensitive probes, 7 days for any probe marked sensitive.
   - Transcripts, tokenized inputs: TTL = 180 days.
   - Human labels and annotation metadata: TTL = 540 days (annotations are more expensive to reproduce).
   - Aggregated metrics/counters: retained indefinitely in compressed form but with no per-request identifiers.

3) Storage protections:
   - All retained artifacts must be encrypted at rest with customer-specific KMS keys when tied to identifiable customers.
   - Access requires IAM-based approval and just-in-time ephemeral credentials for annotators.

Retention Table (defaults)

| Artifact Type | Default TTL | Encryption | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Raw request body (sensitive) | 7 days | Customer KMS | Marked when payload contains sensitive PII or is customer-linked |
| Raw request body (non-sensitive) | 30 days | Platform KMS | e.g., synthetic probes with no IDs |
| Transcript / tokenized input | 180 days | Platform KMS | Useful for debugging and model regression triage |
| Model outputs (per-request) | 180 days | Platform KMS | Strip request identifiers before export |
| Annotations (human labels) | 540 days | Platform KMS | Consider snapshot and archiving before purge |
| Aggregated metrics | Indefinite (compressed) | N/A | No per-request linkage; stored in telemetry-warehouse |

Operational Controls and Enforcement

- Probe Catalog Registration: Every probe set must be registered in the probe-catalog service with metadata: owner, sensitivity flag, expected TTL, privacy budget owner, and estimated storage footprint. The eval-orchestrator rejects scheduling for unregistered probe sets.

- Automated TTL Enforcement: The retention-worker runs daily and performs three actions: (a) mark items for deletion, (b) publish deletion plan to audit-log, (c) execute deletions in batch during a low-cost window (02:00–04:00 PT). Deletions are soft by default (tombstone) for 48 hours to allow emergency recovery via a documented approval flow.

- Privacy budget accounting:
   - For datasets touching live customer data we maintain per-dataset cumulative epsilon as a metadata field in probe-catalog. The privacy-accountant job increments budget when probes are stored or exported. Exports that would exceed configured epsilon are blocked.
   - For DP mechanisms, annotate operators must add the DP parameters used (epsilon, delta) and attach the proof-of-noise job id to the dataset metadata.

Cost guardrails

- Storage caps: Each probe-catalog entry must include a storage cap. If a catalog exceeds 80% of cap, alert to probe-owner and auto-halt new probe ingestion for that catalog.
- Annotation spend SLO: Annotation projects must include a budget and estimated cost-per-label. If monthly spend reaches 90% of the project budget, the annotation pipeline pauses new assignments and notifies the owner.
- Archival policy for cold artifacts: Artifacts older than 90 days and below access thresholds are moved to cold-backed storage (lower cost) with a 30 day retrieval window and an additional retrieval fee applied to owner’s cost center.

Examples (commands and SQL)

- Register a new probe catalog entry (CLI snippet):

  redwood-probe register --name "nlp-safety-suite" --owner-team "ml-quality" --sensitivity "non-sensitive" --ttl 180 --storage-cap "500GB" --privacy-budget "none"

- Query current retention state (SQL):

  SELECT probe_catalog, artifact_type, count(*) AS objects, sum(size_bytes)/pow(1024,3) AS size_gb
  FROM probe_artifacts
  WHERE created_at > '{{date_sub(now(), interval 365 day)}}'
  GROUP BY 1,2;

- Soft-delete workflow (operator steps):
  1) retention-worker marks items and emits deletion_plan:{id} to /audit-log.
  2) Probe owner has 48 hrs to request recovery: redwood-probe recover --plan-id {id} --approval-token {ticket}.
  3) After 48 hrs, deletion-job executes and emits deletion_complete to /audit-log.

Runbook: Emergency Purge (data breach or legal takedown)

1) Trigger: Security or Legal escalation with ticket and owner confirmation.
2) Action: Run emergency-purge job with provided filters (customer_id OR request_id).
   - CLI: redwood-probe emergency-purge --filter "customer_id=12345" --reason "legal-takedown-2024-11" --urgent
3) The job runs immediate hard delete (no soft tombstone). All changes recorded to audit-log and retention-audit S3 bucket.
4) Post-action: Notify Compliance & Legal; rotate KMS keys if keys were suspected compromised; perform snapshot for incident review and then shred it per evidence retention policy.

Monitoring and Alerts

- Metrics to emit:
  - probe_artifacts.total_size_gb (by catalog)
  - probe_artifacts.objects_marked_for_deletion_count
  - annotation.monthly_spend_by_project
  - privacy_budget.remaining_epsilon (by dataset)
  - retention_worker.run_latency_seconds

- Alert rules (examples):
  - Storage cap exceeded: fire if probe_artifacts.total_size_gb > storage_cap * 0.9 for 5m.
  - Annotation budget near limit: fire if annotation.monthly_spend_by_project > budget * 0.9.
  - Unexpected retention-worker failure: fire if retention_worker.run_latency_seconds > 300s or last_success > 24h.

Change Management and Rollouts

- Any change to default TTLs or privacy-budget defaults must go through: (a) proposal (ADR template) -> (b) security review -> (c) staging rollout for 2 weeks -> (d) production rollout with 7-day observation window.
- Owners must update probe-catalog entries when TTLs change; retention-worker supports versioned retention policies so older artifacts respect the policy that was active at creation time unless a forced migration is approved.

Responsibilities and Contacts

- Probe owners (ML teams): ensure registration, set sensitivity flag, supply storage cap and annotation budget.
- Evaluations Platform (owner: eng-applied-ml): implement catalog enforcement, retention-worker, and privacy-accountant.
- SRE: monitor retention-worker, run emergency purges, own archival pipeline.
- Security & Legal: policy approvals for privacy budgets and emergency purges.

Appendix: Operational Checklist for New Probe Catalog

1) Create probe-catalog entry with sensitivity and budget.
2) Confirm storage cap and annotation budget with finance tagging.
3) Verify encryption settings and KMS key assignment.
4) Run small ingest smoke-test and validate retention-worker tombstone appears within 24 hrs.
5) Add alert hooks for storage cap and privacy budget depletion.
